title: Pre-release contingency playbook for API stability and comms
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define a concise, testable contingency playbook for the upcoming runtime-1.22 API release. Scope covers: release blockers detection and triage flows, automated and manual rollback criteria, incident communication templates for internal and customer-facing comms, and cross-team responsibilities (Engineering, SRE, Support, Legal, Sales, and PM). This ticket coordinates owners, artifacts, and verification steps needed to sign off the launch readiness gate. The playbook should be usable as a runbook during the first 72 hours after rollout and evergreen within the Redwood Console playbooks library.
checklist: Finalize release blocker checklist and commit criteria (ENG lead + PM)
Smoke test matrix for critical endpoints (generate, chat, embeddings, rerank)
Automated canary metrics configured in dashboards (latency P50/P95, error rates, token throughput)
Rollback runbook drafted and validated on staging including DB/schema and config toggles
Incident comms templates (internal Slack, customer email, status page) reviewed by Legal and Support
On-call escalation path documented and owners paged in pager duty rotation
Postmortem template created and retention policy agreed with Compliance
Release notes section drafted and opt-in customers flagged for targeted comms

rollback_plan_summary: Primary rollback is an automated traffic split back to runtime-1.21 with feature-flag toggle. If rollback fails (config propagation or incompatibility), fallback is cluster-level draining with emergency autoscale to compensate while SRE performs fast rollback. Rollback steps include: 1) Pause new deployments and freeze config; 2) Switch traffic via routing control plane to previous model version; 3) Verify smoke tests pass on the reverted path; 4) Notify stakeholders via incident comms template; 5) Open a hotfix branch and block release until root cause triaged.
incident_comm_templates: Internal (Slack channel): short issue summary, impact level, immediate mitigation, next steps, owners and expected ETA
Customer-facing (email): plain-language impact statement, affected endpoints, mitigation steps if any, expected timeline, link to status page
Status page update: one-line incident title, user-facing impact, current mitigation, last update timestamp, next ETA
Postmortem public summary: what happened, impact, root cause, short-term mitigation, long-term fix, compensations if applicable
